subject: Sundial Health - post-upgrade surge: latency, errors, throughput drop
messages:
From: Erin Lopez <erin.lopez@sundialhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency and errors after v4.1/quant profile swap

Karthik,

We rolled the v4.1 model + the new qprofile the team recommended into production at ~02:00 PDT and started seeing issues immediately.

Symptoms:
- p95 latencies jumped from ~180ms to 1.2s across hot routes
- error rate (5xx) spiked to ~3.4% (was <0.2%)
- overall throughput dropped ~30% despite constant traffic

We've attached a short error sample and a p99 trace snapshot. We've already rolled back on our side to the previous pinned variant, but we need an explanation and a mitigation plan — Sundial's billing page and core user journeys impacted this morning.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (routing, kernel selection, or cache behavior) around the rollout window? We need an exec-level update in the next 4 hours for our CTO.

Thanks,
Erin Lopez
Head of Platform Operations
Sundial Health

Attachments: error-sample-logs.txt, p99-trace-20260630.png
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Lopez <erin.lopez@sundialhealth.com>
Cc: Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency and errors after v4.1/quant profile swap

Erin — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. I'm very sorry for the disruption.

Short answer: nothing intentional was deployed to Sundial's dedicated pool from Redwood control plane during that window; however, we did push a global kernel-selection heuristic tweak at 01:45 PDT that can change per-model kernel picks (rollout was gated but did reach a subset of fleets). I'm escalating to runtime/quant infra right now to validate if the heuristic produced a sub-optimal kernel + qprofile pairing for v4.1.

Immediate actions I'm taking: 
1) Looping in runtime leads (marissa, ben) and SRE to get thread-level triage.
2) Requesting a full KV/prefix cache hit rate export for your routes (can you confirm the route names and a link to the tracing spans?)
3) Putting together an executive summary for your CTO — ETA ~90m.

I'll keep you updated as we have concrete findings.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erin Lopez <erin.lopez@sundialhealth.com>, Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sundial - post-upgrade surge: latency, errors, throughput drop

Marissa/Ben — escalating to you due to customer impact and exec ask. Summary below and attachments from Sundial.

Summary (short):
- Sundial rolled v4.1 + our recommended qprofile into prod ~02:00 PDT. They immediately observed p95 jump to ~1.2s, 5xx ~3.4%, throughput -30%.
- Customer rolled back to prior pinned variant; still wants an RCA and mitigation plan.
- We rolled a kernel-selection heuristic globally at 01:45 PDT that may have affected model-kernel pairing for certain sequence-length distributions.

What I need from runtime/SRE:
- Verify whether the heuristic caused a different kernel selection for v4.1 on Sundial's pool between 02:00–02:30 PDT.
- Check qprofile runtime behavior: were quantized paths taken and did any fallback to higher-precision kernels occur (that would explain latency spike)?
- Retrieve instance-level GPU utilization and memcpy stats for the affected hosts.
- Confirm whether any autoscaling/fallback routing events coincided with the window.

Customer expects an exec-ready summary in ~4 hours. If we don't have a root cause, be prepared to propose immediate mitigations: revert the heuristic globally, pin Sundial to the prior kernel/qprofile combo, or provide a hotfix qprofile.

Attaching: Sundial's logs (error-sample-logs.txt), p99 trace image (p99-trace-20260630.png), qprofile diff they saved (qprofile-diff.json).

Thanks — prioritize and I'll coordinate the external update.

— Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erin Lopez <erin.lopez@sundialhealth.com>, Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@sundialhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sundial - post-upgrade surge: latency, errors, throughput drop

Karthik — thanks for the escalation. Ben and I will own immediate triage; I'll assemble a short exec summary for our CS and legal teams in parallel.

Initial ask for triage team (Ben, SRE):
- Snapshot kernel assignments and timings for v4.1 models in Sundial's dedicated pool between 01:50–03:30 PDT (include kernel versions).
- Capture qprofile runtime decisions and any exception/fallback logs.
- Run a controlled decode test on a repro input set with the current heuristic on a non-prod replica and compare latencies to baseline.

If we see the heuristic as the culprit we should:
A) Immediately rollback the heuristic (global kill switch available) — note: rollback will momentarily increase scheduling variability but is reversible.
B) Offer Sundial a hotfix qprofile and a golden kernel pin for their critical routes.

Erin/Rajesh — we'll send an interim note to your CTO by 14:30 PDT with what we know. Karthik, loop SRE and runtime infra; Ben, prioritize.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Lopez <erin.lopez@sundialhealth.com>, Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@sundialhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Sundial exec update — interim findings and next steps

Erin/Rajesh — interim update per our investigation this afternoon. 

What we found (interim):
- Kernel-selection heuristic change at 01:45 PDT led to a different kernel assignment for v4.1 in ~64% of Sundial's hot-route traffic during the 02:00–02:20 window. Those kernel variants exercised a quantized decode path that, under the observed sequence-length distribution, triggered additional memcpy operations and a fallback path in the runtime. That explains the observed p95 jump and throughput loss.
- A small percentage (~0.6%) of requests hit an edge-case where a runtime quantization exception surfaced as a 5xx; those have stack traces matching the error samples you provided.

Actions taken so far: 
1) We disabled the heuristic globally at 15:10 PDT (roll back).
2) Pinned Sundial's dedicated pool to the previous kernel/qprofile combo for immediate stability.
3) Preparing a hotfix qprofile that avoids the memcpy-heavy codepath; initial perf runs show p95 returning to ~200ms.

Next steps and timeline: 
- Hotfix qprofile candidate (non-prod): ETA 2h for validation, 4h for staged rollout.
- Postmortem & RCA doc with root cause and timeline: ETA 24h.
- Compensation/credits: Ben, can you work with Sales to propose a goodwill credit for the incident? (Suggested: one week of dedicated capacity credit for June.)

We're deeply sorry for the disruption. We'll share the exec-ready RCA and proposed credits as soon as Ben and CS align. Please tell your CTO they can reach me directly for any clarifications.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: qprofile-diff.json (customer), internal incident ticket: https://redwood.app/ops/incident/SD-2026-0472
